text:
maria: quick heads-up — noticed p99 spikes after we flipped to small-burst policy (microbatch=2) for streaming chat on pool-3 this morning. p50 looks fine but p99 jumps to ~1.2s. non-streamed completions with same mb=2 config don't show the spike. anyone seen this?

arjun: do you have numbers and kernel info? streaming vs sync paths use different kernels, could be a kernel fallback.

maria: yeah quick numbers from 08:10–08:25 UTC: streaming (mb=2) qps=170, p50=48ms, p95=180ms, p99=1200ms, kvcache hit=72%
non-streamed (mb=2) qps=160, p50=52ms, p95=190ms, p99=260ms, kvcache hit=75%
kernel hints: streaming used kernel_group=stream_v2 -> fallback to stream_v1 on some batches per logs

nick: that delta is suspicious. streaming path likely doing extra per-client flush/commit work on tiny batches — tail work adds up. plus kernel fallback is expensive. did you catch a perf trace?

maria: not full perf yet, but stack traces show repeated kernel load/evict on the same GPU during the p99 windows. infra-bot printed these lines: "kernel_load_ms=12, kernel_swap_ms=45, kv_evictions=4" a bunch of times.

infra-bot: system alert: pool-3 GPU memory pressure spiked at 08:13:21 UTC; ephemeral KV spills observed. trace_id=trace-1725000000-08:13

arjun: please run a short canary with NVTX and the perf counters: 
```
sh run_perf.sh --pool pool-3 --trace trace-1725000000 --nvtx --perf-events cycles,stalled-cycles-frontend,cache-misses --duration 300
```
Also include kernel_dump and kvstats.

lisa: two hypotheses: 1) small microbatches increase frequency of KV cache misses per-client because we miss aggregation opportunities (batches too small to coalesce prefixes), so more KV eviction/spill work during streaming; 2) the streaming runtime does extra per-request websocket/frame bookkeeping on emit which becomes visible only at tail. Non-streamed completions aggregate more before final emit, so less tail overhead.

nick: agree. also we have a known regression where stream_v2 falls back to generic_kernel for mb <=3 when sequence_length variance is high — fallback path loads extra kernels and does a sync. that would explain p99 gulf.

maria: here's the experiment config I used: 
```json
{
  "policy": "small-burst",
  "microbatch_size": 2,
  "streaming": true,
  "kernel_hint": "auto",
  "kv_prefetch": false,
  "per_client_mb": false
}
```

arjun: try these quick mitigations in a canary: 1) kernel_hint: prefer_stream_v1 (avoid fallback), 2) kv_prefetch=true for short seqs, 3) adaptive per-client fill: allow up to 8 for the same websocket if idle window <200ms. config snippet: 
```json
{
  "adaptive_mb": {"min":2, "max":8, "policy":"per_client_fill"},
  "kv_prefetch": true,
  "kernel_hint": "prefer_stream_v1"
}
```

lisa: other low-risk option: increase kv cache TTL for short-lived keys so we reduce eviction churn during bursts. set kv_ttl_ms=120000 for canary.

maria: starting a canary w/ those three changes on pool-3-canary now (trace id trace-1725000000-canary). will run 15m and post results.

(10m later)
maria: quick result after 15m: streaming canary qps ~165, p50=50ms, p95=170ms, p99=320ms, kvcache hit=89%. no kernel fallback events in logs.

arjun: nice — that strongly points to fallback + kv churn. can you also run a >1h run to ensure no regression at higher traffic? and bump seq variance to stress kernel selector.

nick: agree, also file a follow-up to remove the aggressive fallback when mb<=3 until we have improved kernel swap perf. put a test in kernel-selector to avoid fallback if gpu_mem_pressure>0.2.

lisa: will open a small RFC for 'streaming microbatch heuristics' — propose default adaptive_mb per-client and kv_prefetch=true for streaming with short seqs. include the perf traces.

maria: thanks all — canary looks good, rolling the canary config to 10% on pool-3. will watch traces and alert if p99 creeps. :thumbsup:

nick: nice triage, great cross-team debug. :rocket:
